title: Greet and introduce yourself / Fiiɗe e jom suɓe
bridge: Fiiɗe e jom suɓe, nder español, mbaɗanɗe naaɗaa 'Hola' ko 'Buenos días', e fiiɗe e jom suɓe naaɗaa 'Me llamo...' ko 'Soy...'. Nder ingglis, koɗo eɗaa 'Hello' ko 'Good morning', e fiiɗe e jom suɓe naaɗaa 'My name is...' ko 'I am...'. Laaɗo jiiɗo eɗaa ingglis ko 'I am called...' (ɗum ko ɓurtaani eɗaa, wonaaɗaa jiiɗo eɗaa eɓɓe eɗaa eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe). Koɗo eɗaa ingglis, mbaɗanɗe naaɗaa 'to be' eɗaa e jom suɓe: 'What is your name?' (ko 'How are you called?' ɗum ɓurtaani eɗaa).
rule: Fiiɗe e jom suɓe: 'Hello' (Hola), 'Hi' (ɓurtaani eɗaa), 'Good morning' (Buenos días), 'Good afternoon' (Buenas tardes), 'Good evening' (Buenas noches al llegar). Fiiɗe e jom suɓe: 'My name is...' (Me llamo...) ko 'I am...' (Soy...). Jom suɓe e jom suɓe: 'What is your name?' (¿Cómo te llamas?). Jom suɓe e jom suɓe: 'Nice to meet you' (Encantado/a de conocerte) e jom suɓe e jom suɓe: 'Nice to meet you too'. Jom suɓe e jom suɓe: 'Goodbye', 'Bye', 'See you later'.

common_error.explanation: Nder español, mbaɗanɗe naaɗaa 'Me llamo Anna', ɗum ingglis, laaɗo jiiɗo eɗaa eɓɓe eɗaa e jom suɓe 'My name is...' ko 'I am...'. 'I am called' ɗum ɓurtaani eɗaa, wonaaɗaa jiiɗo eɗaa eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe.

common_error.explanation: Nder esañol, mbaɗanɗe naaɗaa 'Me llamo Anna', ɗum ingglis, laaɗo jiiɗo eɗaa eɓɓe eɗaa e jom suɓe 'My name is...' ko 'I am...'. 'I am called' ɗum ɓurtaani eɗaa, wonaaɗaa jiiɗo eɗaa eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe eɓɓe.

title: Give personal information (age, nationality, profession) / Naani dowli (jom, leñol, dewtere)
bridge: En pulaar, jom dowli jom 25 no heewi (wonaa 'heewi' nden), eɗen ingiilisi heewi 'I am 25 years old' (wonaa 'heewi' nden). Eɗen leñol, ingiilisi heewi 'I am Spanish' (wonaa article). Eɗen dewtere, ingiilisi heewi 'I am a teacher' (article 'a').
rule: Jom dowli: 'I am [number] years old' (ej: I am 25 years old). Leñol: 'I am [nationality]' (ej: I am Spanish, I am Mexican). Dewtere: 'I am a/an [profession]' (ej: I am a doctor, I am an engineer). Nden: 'How old are you?' (Jom dowli ma?), 'Where are you from?' (Fan ma joota?), 'What do you do?' (Dewtere ma?) o 'What is your job?'.

common_error.explanation: En pulaar, jom dowli heewi 'Jom dowli 25 no heewi', eɗen ingiilisi heewi 'to be' laawo dowli.

title: Describe objects and people (basic) / Describe objetos y personas (básico)
bridge: E Pulaar, to describe objects and people, we place the adjective after the noun: 'puccu balewa', 'debbo woota'. In English, the adjective comes BEFORE the noun: 'a red car', 'a tall girl'. We also use the verb 'to be' for general descriptions (She is tall) and 'have got' for physical characteristics (She has got blue eyes).
rule: To describe: 1) Adjective + noun (a big house). 2) Subject + verb 'to be' + adjective (The house is big). 3) Subject + 'have/has got' + characteristic (She has got long hair). Common adjectives: big (large), small (suntu), tall (toowta), short (suntu), beautiful (jomma), old (jomma), young (yeehi), fast (sappo), slow (sappo).

common_error.explanation: E Pulaar, the adjective comes after the noun ('puccu balewa'), but in English it comes BEFORE the noun ('a red car'). This is one of the most common errors for Spanish speakers.

examples.note: The adjective comes before the noun.
We use 'to be' for general descriptions.
We use 'have got' for physical characteristics.

examples.original: My brother is young and he has got green eyes.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ ˈbrʌðə ɪz jʌŋ ænd hiː hæz ɡɒt ɡriːn aɪz/
examples.translation: Yimre am naani toowta e naani yitere ndane.
